findings.quote: The attractions between solute and solvent must be about as strong as the ones broken.
findings.problem: The 'must be about as strong' condition is false when the solute-solvent attractions are much stronger than the ones broken. That case dissolves well, often with heat given off: HCl gas in water is one example, and many very soluble salts are another. A student who learns this rule will wrongly conclude that much stronger solute-solvent attractions stop a substance from dissolving. The correct condition is that the new attractions are about as strong as, or stronger than, the ones broken. Entropy can also let a substance dissolve when the new attractions are a little weaker. No earlier round raised this sentence.
findings.source: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 11.1, The Dissolution Process (much stronger solvation gives a strongly exothermic process and high solubility; disorder lets endothermic dissolution occur); reader-rules.md, Added after the Sol audit

findings.quote: If they are not, the bonds differ in length.
findings.problem: The round-4 fix added this converse, and it is not true in general. A set of resonance structures that are not all equivalent can still give equal bonds when the molecule is symmetric. Benzene drawn with two Kekule structures and three Dewar structures has six equal C-C bonds. Sulfate drawn with an all-single-bond structure and several S=O structures has four equal S-O bonds, about 149 pm each. CO2 drawn as O=C=O plus two triple-bond structures has two equal C-O bonds. The sentence also does not say which bonds it means. What is true is that equivalent structures give equal bonds, and structures that are not equivalent contribute unequally, so bonds may differ, as the C-O and N-N bonds in HN3 do. The case is narrow, but the sentence states a false rule about the resonance item, which the brief places at official curriculum class (dost-sei-L106).
findings.source: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, section 7.4, Formal Charges and Resonance; reader-rules.md, Added after the Sol audit

findings.quote: Some species need **resonance**. Two or more valid Lewis structures use the same atom order but differ in where the double or triple bonds and lone pairs sit.
findings.problem: This paragraph has five sentences, and the limit is one to three short sentences. The round-4 fix made the paragraph longer.
